body.statement: For the known-uniform-design class \(\mathcal M(d,m,\alpha,\beta,s,L)\), determine the explicit piecewise sequence \(r_n^{\star}(d,m,\alpha,\beta,s,L)\), including every unavoidable critical logarithmic factor, and instantiate \(\widehat Q_{\mathrm{HO}}\) so that \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal M(d,m,\alpha,\beta,s,L)}E_P[W_1(\widehat Q_{\mathrm{HO}},Q_1)]\asymp R_n(d,m,\alpha,\beta,s,L)\asymp r_n^{\star}(d,m,\alpha,\beta,s,L)\). Characterize by a necessary-and-sufficient condition on \((d,m,\alpha,\beta,s)\) when \(r_n^{\star}\asymp r_{\mathrm{or},n}(m,s)\), and derive the sharp rate in every non-oracle region by matching same-class all-estimator converses.
body.justification: The exact full frontier, rather than an oracle-only upper bound or isolated lower bound, is the publishable theorem-level kernel.
body.gap: No cited result gives the full known-uniform-design nuisance frontier: LuedtkeFukumizu2025DoubleGen explicitly leaves nuisance-difficulty lower bounds open in its broader framework, NilesWeedBerthet2022 has direct samples, and the inaccessible Kennedy2023ACIC announcement does not expose a loss, formula, model, or proof that can subsume this marginal multivariate \(W_1\) target.
body.consumer: The frontier supplies DoubleGen and DecFM with a known-uniform-design benchmark that isolates rough propensity and conditional-law difficulty, plus a positive reconstruction target; extrapolation to their unknown-design settings is outside the theorem.

obligation.what_is_open: The matching achievability rate and all-regime converse, including critical logarithms and the asymmetric regime in which the shared-propensity leakage term dominates.
obligation.obstruction: The interaction lower envelope is rigorous, but matching it requires the unresolved high-rank coefficient certificate or a different estimator. Conversely, the present shared-sign mixture alone does not certify every asymmetric regime or any critical multiscale logarithm. No honest optimization of unproved coefficient bounds can determine the sharp frontier.
obligation.attempted: Derived the full shared-sign mixture calculation, the representative strict separation, the oracle submodel rate, and the signed-to-probability projection. Also optimized an explicit clipped propensity-series inverse-weighted estimator to obtain a loose same-class upper rate; this does not exploit outcome smoothness and therefore does not match the lower side in general.
obligation.partial_result:
There is nevertheless an explicit loose same-class bracket.  Split the sample in half.  On the first half, estimate \(e\) by its empirical coefficients in a fixed boundary-wavelet space of dimension \(K\asymp n^{d/(2\alpha+d)}\), and clip the resulting series to \([1/4,3/4]\).  Orthogonality, Bernoulli variance bounded by \(1/4\), Hölder approximation, and pointwise nonexpansiveness of clipping give
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal M}E_P\lVert\widehat e-e\rVert_{L_1}
 \leq C\left(K^{-\alpha/d}+\sqrt{K/n}\right)
 \leq Cn^{-\alpha/(2\alpha+d)}.
 \tag{23}
\]
On the second half define the probability-valued, normalized inverse-propensity estimator
\[
 \widehat Q_{\mathrm{IPW}}
 :=\frac{\sum_i A_i\widehat e(X_i)^{-1}\delta_{Y_i}}
          {\sum_i A_i\widehat e(X_i)^{-1}},
\]
with a fixed point mass on the event of a zero denominator.  Conditional on the first half, all weights are at most four.  Symmetrization followed by the dyadic entropy bound for one-Lipschitz functions on \([0,1]^m\) gives, for \(m>2\), a weighted empirical-process term at most \(Cn^{-1/m}\).  For every anchored one-Lipschitz \(f\), its conditional bias is
\[
 \left|\int_{\mathcal X}\left\{\frac{e(x)}{\widehat e(x)}-1\right\}
       E\{f(Y)\mid A=1,X=x\}\,dx\right|
 \leq4\sqrt m\,\lVert\widehat e-e\rVert_{L_1}.
\]
The same calculation with the constant function controls the normalizing denominator; its lower-tail contribution is bounded by the diameter \(\sqrt m\).  Equations (23) and Kantorovich--Rubinstein duality therefore yield
\[
 R_n(d,m,\alpha,\beta,s,L)
 \leq C\left(n^{-1/m}+n^{-\alpha/(2\alpha+d)}\right).
 \tag{24}
\]
Together with \(\texttt{thm:interaction-lower-envelope}\) and \(\texttt{prop:oracle-randomized-reduction}\), this gives the honest bracket
\[
 c\max\left\{r_{\mathrm{or},n}(m,s),
              \underline r_n(d,m,\alpha,\beta,s,L)\right\}-Ce^{-cn}
 \leq R_n(d,m,\alpha,\beta,s,L)
 \leq C\left(n^{-1/m}+n^{-\alpha/(2\alpha+d)}\right).
 \tag{25}
\]
The two sides do not match in general, so (25) does not determine the sharp frontier or its critical logarithms.
